mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has improved monotonically from -17.1% to -13.6% over four weeks, indicating a consistent recovery trend. This trend will persist over the next four weeks, driving RETAIL_REC further above the baseline mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved 3.5 percentage points over four weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or reverses by more than 2 percentage points in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has stabilized near -12% to -13%, indicating employers have reached a steady-state remote-work equilibrium. This stability removes downward pressure on retail demand, allowing RETAIL_REC to continue its recovery trajectory independent of further workplace changes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES week-on-week change falls below 1 percentage point in absolute value
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES ranged only -14.9% to -12.3% across four weeks
failure_condition: WORKPLACES declines by more than 2 percentage points in any single week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve relative to its four-week mean.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT station usage remains severely depressed at -35% to -39%, constraining access to retail districts. If TRANSIT recovers by more than 5 percentage points in any single week, it will unlock retail footfall, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the following two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT week-on-week improvement exceeds 5 percentage points
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT at -35.3% in t-0w, historically -36% to -39%
failure_condition: TRANSIT improves by more than 5 percentage points in a single week but RETAIL_REC does not increase in the following two weeks, or TRANSIT remains below -30% throughout the forecast period.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined from +8.0% to +5.6% over four weeks, indicating reduced home confinement. This behavioral shift toward outdoor activity is coupled with PARKS stabilizing near 0%, suggesting consumers are reallocating time from residential to retail-recreation venues rather than parks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls below 6% while PARKS remains within ±2% of zero
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL declined 2.4 points over four weeks
fact:PARKS near zero in t-1w and t-0w
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL does not fall below 6% or PARKS surges above +5%, or RETAIL_REC declines over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has stabilized at -3% to -5%, indicating essential shopping patterns are locked in. This stability signals consumer confidence in supply chains, removing a constraint on discretionary retail visits, allowing RETAIL_REC to recover.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM ranged only -5.3% to -3.3% across four weeks
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM falls below -8% in any week over the next four weeks, or RETAIL_REC declines relative to its baseline.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility has recovered from -11.1% to -0.9% over three weeks, then declined slightly to -0.9%, indicating outdoor recreation demand is near saturation. Consumers will shift from parks to retail-recreation venues, driving RETAIL_REC upward over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS stabilizes within ±2% of zero for two consecutive weeks
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS improved from -11.1% to -0.9% in three weeks
failure_condition: PARKS surges above +5% in any week, or RETAIL_REC fails to improve relative to its four-week mean over the next four weeks.

mechanism_narrative: Mid-September in Sydney marks the onset of spring school holidays and spring shopping season. RETAIL_REC recovery from -17.1% to -13.6% reflects early seasonal demand. This seasonal effect will accelerate RETAIL_REC recovery over the next four weeks independent of other mobility signals.
evidence_refs: fact:Decision date is 2020-09-15, spring season onset
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not exceed the mean of the last 28 days, or declines by more than 1 percentage point in any single week.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT remains severely depressed at -35% while WORKPLACES stabilizes at -12%, indicating a bifurcated labor market: remote workers do not commute, but office workers face transit constraints. If TRANSIT fails to recover above -30% within two weeks, retail footfall will remain suppressed, preventing RETAIL_REC from exceeding its current trajectory.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT remains below -30% for two consecutive weeks while WORKPLACES stays between -14% and -11%
failure_condition: TRANSIT recovers above -30% in any single week, or RETAIL_REC improves by more than 2 percentage points relative to its four-week mean over the next four weeks.
